Baseline: each 48 V actuator programme — EPS (ASIL D for loss/unintended assist), active roll (typically ASIL B-C), rear-axle steer (ASIL C-D), e-compressor (QM/ASIL A) — develops its own motor-drive safety work products: technical safety concept, hardware FMEDA, dependent failure analysis, software safety requirements for current/position monitoring, safety-related HIL test suites and confirmation reviews/assessments, even where the power stage, gate driver, MCU safety mechanisms and FOC software core are similar. ideaData.title: One ISO 26262 SEooC safety case for the 48 V motor-drive core, reused four times
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: each 48 V actuator programme — EPS (ASIL D for loss/unintended assist), active roll (typically ASIL B-C), rear-axle steer (ASIL C-D), e-compressor (QM/ASIL A) — develops its own motor-drive safety work products: technical safety concept, hardware FMEDA, dependent failure analysis, software safety requirements for current/position monitoring, safety-related HIL test suites and confirmation reviews/assessments, even where the power stage, gate driver, MCU safety mechanisms and FOC software core are similar. ISO 26262 provides the Safety Element out of Context (SEooC) route for exactly this: elements developed for reuse under stated assumptions of use; suppliers can reuse safety analyses and architecture evaluations across applications, cutting cost and improving consistency, while developing everything to ASIL D for low-ASIL uses is costly. Proposal: define a 48 V motor-drive core SEooC at two integrity tiers (ASIL D tier for EPS/rear steer, ASIL B tier for roll/compressor), with documented assumptions of use (supply range per LV 148, safe states, fault-tolerant time intervals ≥ 10 ms), developed once with an independent assessment; each actuator programme then performs only the validation of assumptions and the application-specific delta analyses. Builds on the library's hardware commonisation (one 48 V half-bridge power cell) and the ASIL-decomposition idea, extending them to the work products.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Safety analyses, confirmation measures and safety-test campaigns are paid once per tier instead of once per actuator; each programme pays only for assumption validation and delta work. Amortised engineering per vehicle falls.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: No plant impact. Engineering organisation: a platform safety team owns the SEooC; programme teams consume it. Supplier contracts reference the SEooC safety manual.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Hardware and software core configuration-controlled; deviations require formal change impact analysis. Reduces variant-specific diagnostics, which also simplifies dealer diagnostic trees.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Medium — engineering amortised per vehicle
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cost-bridge lines net €8.75 per vehicle (Safety analyses (FMEDA/FTA/DFA): 5.00; Confirmation measures (assessments/audits): 1.00; Safety-related HIL test campaigns: 4.00; SEooC maintenance and configuration control: -1.25). Engineering costs amortised over 200,000 MHEV vehicles (4 years × 50,000); costs are estimates of supplier/OEM engineering recovered in piece price or programme budgets.

Proof: ISO 26262-10 SEooC process, independent functional safety assessment per tier, per-programme assumption verification report, confirmation review. Mitigation: two tiers rather than one ASIL D for all.

engineering.mechanism: Engineering cost per vehicle = Σ programme safety cost / vehicles. Baseline for four drives: FMEDA/FTA/DFA ~€0.8M each (€3.2M), confirmation measures ~€0.25M each (€1.0M), safety HIL campaigns ~€0.5M each (€2.0M) = €6.2M over 200,000 vehicles = €31/vehicle. SEooC: two-tier core analyses €1.2M + 4 × €0.25M deltas = €2.2M; confirmation €0.4M + 4 × €0.1M = €0.8M; HIL core €0.6M + 4 × €0.15M = €1.2M; plus SEooC maintenance €0.25M. The fault-tolerant time interval assumption (≥ 10 ms) is the key technical boundary: EPS unintended-torque FTTI ~10-20 ms, roll ~50-100 ms, compressor non-critical.
engineering.specDeltas: New deliverables: SEooC safety manual per tier (assumptions of use: 48 V supply 36-54 V operating per LV 148, safe states = torque-off/short-circuit braking, FTTI ≥ 10 ms, MCU lockstep for ASIL D tier), core FMEDA (SPFM ≥ 99 % / LFM ≥ 90 % for D tier; ≥ 90 %/60 % for B tier), core DFA, software safety requirements for current/position plausibility, reusable HIL test suite. Per programme: assumption-of-use verification report, delta FMEDA, integration test. Deleted: four stand-alone drive-level analyses and test campaigns.
engineering.validationPlan: Independent functional safety assessment of each SEooC tier (ISO 26262-2 confirmation measures), audit of SEooC development process. Per programme: confirmation review of assumption verification, integration testing on HIL (fault injection: phase open/short, sensor stuck, supply over/under-voltage per LV 148), vehicle-level validation per item. Regulatory: R79 documentation for EPS references SEooC manual. No PPAP impact beyond normal product releases.
engineering.dfmImplications: No physical part change; configuration management of the core across four suppliers or one platform supplier, run by a change control board with impact analysis on every core change. Common diagnostics and fault codes reduce dealer tool variants and technician training.
engineering.costBridge: Per vehicle (amortised over 200,000 vehicles): safety analyses €16.00 → €11.00; confirmation measures €5.00 → €4.00; safety HIL campaigns €10.00 → €6.00; SEooC maintenance adds €1.25. Not included: hardware commonisation savings (separate library idea) and product-liability effects.

ideaData.title: 48 V battery designed for 8-minute dismantling and closed-loop take-back, cutting end-of-life provisions
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: the producer of a 48 V battery carries end-of-life obligations (collection, treatment, recycling-efficiency targets) under EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542, whose category depends on whether the 48 V MHEV battery is treated as an SLI battery (starting, lighting, ignition, also auxiliary use) or an EV battery (traction in hybrid vehicles of category M) — a determination for legal review. Typical 48 V packs are partly bonded (adhesive cell fixation, potting on electronics, glued lids), so recyclers dismantle them manually in ~20-30 min or shred them whole with lower-value mixed output; provisions per pack must cover dismantling, DG transport of collected packs and net treatment cost after material credits. Proposal: design rules for disassembly — cells held by compression bands and screws (no adhesive), electronics bay screwed and unpotted (compatible with the repair-bay idea), lid opening via a defined cut line where hot-plate welded, aluminium busbars laser-welded to cell terminals with marked cut zones, polymer parts labelled per ISO 11469 — targeting ≤ 8 min manual dismantling to clean fractions (cells, aluminium, copper, PCB, plastics); plus a closed-loop take-back contract that collects ELV and warranty packs in the returnable P903 totes used inbound. Packs that pass SOH grading can be used as refurbished service units; the rest go to hydrometallurgical recycling at better rates because fractions are clean.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Shorter dismantling, cleaner fractions (higher net material credit) and reuse of inbound DG packaging for returns lower the end-of-life cost the producer must provision per vehicle sold.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Pack assembly: adhesive dispensing deleted (replaced by bands/screws already proposed in the library for the stack), electronics not potted, labels added; small increase in screw count. Recycler contract and reverse logistics set up.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Disassembly sequence documented and tested; cut lines and screw points marked; no adhesive or potting in the cell stack. Same features support dealer repair.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Low-Medium — provisions per vehicle, realised at end of life
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cost-bridge lines net €7.30 per vehicle (Recycler dismantling: 5.50; Net treatment fee after material credit: 1.80; DG transport of collected packs: 0.80; Design-for-disassembly features (net): -0.80). Range −15 %/+10 % for estimate uncertainty: €6.21-€8.03 × 50,000 MHEV vehicles/yr = €311K-€401K. Undiscounted provision per vehicle sold; actual cash flows occur 10-15 years later.

ideaData.riskNotes: Risks: regulatory category uncertainty changes obligations and timing; provisions are discounted far-future costs; screwed joints must still pass vibration and crash. Proof: ISO 16750-3 vibration and mechanical shock on the adhesive-free stack, UN 38.3, dismantling time study with recycler (n = 10 packs), legal opinion on battery category. Mitigation: provisions reviewed yearly.

engineering.mechanism: Dismantling cost = time × recycler labour rate: 25 min × ~€0.36/min (loaded, incl. DG facility) ≈ €9.00 → 8 min ≈ €3.50 incl. setup. Net treatment cost = process cost − material credit; clean fractions raise credit because aluminium housing and copper/aluminium busbars sell as sorted scrap and the cell fraction has less plastic/adhesive contamination (lower hydromet reagent and handling cost). Transport: collected packs travel as UN 3480 (or damaged-battery provisions); returnable totes amortised inbound make the return leg cheaper than one-way DG packaging.
engineering.specDeltas: Delete: structural adhesive between cells and housing (~40 g), electronics potting (~60 g silicone). Add: dismantling drawing with cut line on welded lid (groove 0.5 mm), 6 screws marked, cell-terminal cut zones marked on busbars, ISO 11469 polymer codes, QR link to dismantling instructions (also for battery passport). Contract: take-back with recycler, collected packs returned in the inbound tote loop; SOH grading criteria for refurbished service units (capacity ≥ 85 %, DCR ≤ 1.3× BOL).
engineering.validationPlan: Pack re-validation for adhesive-free stack: ISO 16750-3 vibration, mechanical shock, UN 38.3 T1-T8, LV 148 electrical, n = 3-6 per test. Dismantling time study with recycler, 10 packs, target ≤ 8 min to five fractions. Legal: category determination under 2023/1542 and EPR scheme registration per member state. Refurbished units: OEM service-part qualification (EOL test as new). PPAP for battery design change.
engineering.dfmImplications: Adhesive and potting stations deleted at pack assembly (cycle −30 s); +2 screws per pack. Clearer service and recycling documentation; same tooling for housings with added cut-line groove.
engineering.costBridge: Undiscounted per vehicle: recycler dismantling €9.00 → €3.50; net treatment fee after material credit €6.00 → €4.20; DG transport of collected packs €3.20 → €2.40 using the tote loop; design for disassembly (screws, labels, cut line, net of deleted adhesive/potting) adds €0.80. Not included: discounting, revenue from refurbished service units.
